transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Sofia Ramirez, AE at Redwood. with me is Ethan, our SE, and Maya from CSM.
[00:10] Dr. Alan: Hi, Alan here. Thanks. we want to nail down the evaluation criteria for the POC and make sure it maps to our clinical QA needs.
[00:18] Ethan: Great. high-level we'll scope success criteria, workload sample size, run bench marks, and then a quality evaluation plan with golden prompts and regression tests.
[00:26] Priya: timeline is tight; regulators want evidence of low hallucination rates and JSON schema conformance for downstream systems.
[00:33] Tom: Also cost sensitivity — we have an internal cap on monthly inference spend for the POC.
[00:38] Sofia: Totally. let me outline the success criteria we usually see: p95 latency target, throughput target (req/s), correctness on golden set, and hallucination rate under a threshold. for this POC we propose: p95 <= 200ms for short responses, throughput 50 req/s on reserved workload, and >= 95% pass rate on golden prompts with hallucination < 2%. thoughts?
[00:55] Priya: p95 200ms maybe aggressive for our longer summaries. can we specify by path? short-clinical-check vs long discharge summary.
[01:03] Ethan: yes we should split by route. propose: single-turn quick checks p95 <= 200ms, long summary p95 <= 800ms. also note that latency depends on model variant and quantization — e.g. 8-bit quant can help.
[01:17] Dr. Alan: accuracy metric? what does pass mean for golden prompts? exact match? fuzzy?
[01:23] Maya: we usually do a hybrid: automated scoring plus human review. automated checks include format validation (JSON schema), entity matching for critical PHI fields, and semantic similarity score threshold (e.g., BERTScore or intent F1). any output failing automated checks gets flagged for human review and counts towards hallucination/failure rate.
[01:40] Priya: that seems reasonable. for hallucination we need entity-level verification — if the model invents a medication or lab value that's a hard fail.
[01:49] Ethan: implementation detail: regression tests will include the golden prompt set (100 examples initially) and a separate 1k-sample holdout for drift/regression. golden prompts get expected outputs or structured validators. regression tests run nightly during the POC and after every model change.
[02:03] Tom: how do we score free-text vs structured responses?
[02:07] Sofia: structured responses use strict schema validation + entity match for required fields. free-text uses a combined score: semantic similarity + factuality checks + human spot-checks. we can provide a scoring rubric: pass if combined score >= 0.8 and no hallucinated critical entities.
[02:22] Priya: what about hallucination detection automated? we have some internal diffusion detectors but they throw false positives.
[02:28] Ethan: we'll use a combination: rule-based entity whitelist/blacklist for critical fields, and a classifier for hallucination that flags low-confidence claims, plus human review. for clinical PII/PHI we always prefer strict matching.
[02:40] Dr. Alan: OK. let's talk workload sizing — here's what we can provide: two weeks of anonymized prompt logs, roughly 25k prompts, 70% are short intent classification, 20% structured extraction, 10% long summarizations. top 50 prompt templates cover 85% of traffic.
[02:58] Sofia: perfect. for benchmarking we'll sample proportionally: run a 10k-sample baseline (stratified by traffic type) to measure p95, p50, tokens/sec, and cost projection scaled to your expected monthly volume.
[03:11] Ethan: quick note on caching and batching — Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching; some of Priya's templates might get high cache hit rates which will lower cost and improve latency. we'll capture cache hit rate and effective token savings in the benchmark report. sometimes transcripts show 'KV cash' in notes, apologize typos.
[03:27] Priya: timeline?
[03:29] Sofia: propose: Week 0-1: setup and security review (share SOC2 docs, SAML, KMS integration options). Week 2: receive logs and run baseline benchmarks. Week 3-4: build golden prompt set, run regression and hallucination tests, human review. Week 5: POC review and decision. ~5 weeks total.
[03:48] Tom: acceptable. what are pass/fail thresholds?
[03:51] Ethan: suggested thresholds: golden set pass >= 95% automated+human, hallucination rate < 2% on golden set, structured schema conformance 99.5%, p95 latencies as discussed by route. cost per 1M tokens within your specified cap or within X% of projected.
[04:09] Dr. Alan: for the golden prompts, would Redwood produce expected outputs or do we provide them?
[04:13] Sofia: hybrid — you provide canonical expected outputs for clinical-critical prompts; Redwood will produce baseline outputs and we will co-curate expected responses and edge cases. we'll maintain a living golden set in a shared spreadsheet.
[04:24] Priya: regression cadence? nightly seems fine during POC but want alerts on degradations.
[04:29] Maya: we'll set up automated nightly runs and a dashboard that shows pass rate, p95, hallucination flags, and will email weekly summaries or alerts on thresholds.
[04:39] Ethan: bench specifics: we'll report p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batching efficiency (avg batch size), cache hit rate, and projected monthly cost at your traffic levels. We'll also test quantized variants for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:53] Tom: any security gating? SSO, SAML, audit logs?
[04:57] Sofia: yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem and we can demo RBAC, SAML SSO and KMS for key management. for Hosted POC we can provide SOC2 details and workspace-level audit logs. we'll include security docs in the next email.
[05:10] Dr. Alan: what about the hallucination scoring — what's the actual scoring function?
[05:14] Ethan: scoring breakdown we propose: structured schema checks (weight 0.4), entity factuality (0.3), semantic similarity (0.2), human spot-check adjustment (0.1). combined score >= 0.8 passes. hallucinated critical entities force a fail regardless of combined score.
[05:29] Priya: can you show an example?
[05:31] Ethan: yes later in the follow-up we'll send a sample scoring calc: e.g., structured pass=1.0, entity match=0.9, semantic sim=0.82, human sample adjustment=0.95 => combined weighted = 0.4*1 + 0.3*0.9 + 0.2*0.82 + 0.1*0.95 = ~0.93 pass.
[05:47] Sofia: recap of action items and timeline — we'll send POC agreement and pricing, Priya will send logs, Ethan to run baseline, Dr. Alan to curate golden prompts. next call in two weeks to review bench results.
[05:58] Tom: ok thanks all.
[06:00] Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links to a shared spreadsheet for the golden set and a benchmark schedule. bye.
